paragraphs.text: This psalm seems to have been composed as a form of prayer against the dangers that the Church was in, in the days of Jehoshaphat.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: He calls them God's enemies, who are enemies of his Church.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: The elect of God are his secret ones: for he hides them in the secret of his tabernacle, and preserves them from all dangers.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: They were not content to take the Church as prisoner: but sought to utterly destroy it.
paragraphs.label: d
paragraphs.anchor: cut them off from being a

paragraphs.text: They thought to have subverted your counsel in which the constancy of the Church was established.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: The wickedness of the Ammonites and Moabites is described in that they provoked these other nations to fight against the Israelites.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: By these examples they were confirmed that God would not permit his people to be completely destroyed, Jud 7:21,4:15.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: That is, Judea: for where his Church is, there he dwells among them.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: Because the reprobate could by no means be amended, he prays that they may utterly be destroyed, be unstable and led by all winds.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: That is, be compelled by your plagues to confess your power.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: Though they do not believe, yet they may prove by experience, that it is in vain to resist against your counsel in establishing your Church.
paragraphs.label: n
